articles.title: India and the EU Just Signed the Biggest Free Trade Deal in History. It Took 20 Years.
articles.excerpt: The 'mother of all deals' creates a free trade zone of 2 billion people, slashes car tariffs from 110% to 10%, and reshapes India's position in a fracturing global trade order.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Fed Official Just Said What Markets Were Dreading. India Has the Most to Lose.
articles.excerpt: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warns the central bank may need to raise interest rates soon. For India, already bleeding foreign capital, a rate hike would accelerate the rupee's slide and force the RBI into an impossible choice.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Hits $97 as Iran Fires Missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain. The Deal Everyone Was Waiting For Is Nowhere Close.
articles.excerpt: Fresh hostilities erupt overnight as Iranian missiles target Gulf states. Brent jumps past $97. Diplomacy has stalled. And the world's largest commodity trader says the market is still underpricing the risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Factories Just Had Their Best Month Since February. The War Is Making Everything More Expensive.
articles.excerpt: Manufacturing PMI climbed to 55.0 in May on strong domestic demand, but input costs are at a near four-year high as the Hormuz disruption drives up fuel and material prices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adani Portfolio Just Spent ₹1.53 Lakh Crore in a Single Year. No Indian Company Has Ever Invested That Much.
articles.excerpt: Record capex of $16.1 billion, an $82 billion asset base, and the opening of Navi Mumbai airport mark what the group calls an inflection point.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Missiles Hit Kuwait and Bahrain as Iran War Flares Again. Millions of Indian Workers Are in the Danger Zone.
articles.excerpt: Air raid sirens sounded across both countries as Iranian ballistic missiles and drones targeted Gulf states. Over a million Indians live in Kuwait alone.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Crude Exports Just Hit a Record. Asia Is Buying Everything America Can Ship. It Is Not Nearly Enough.
articles.excerpt: American crude shipments surged to 5.6 million barrels per day in May as Asian refiners scramble for alternatives to Middle Eastern supply. But with 10 million barrels per day still locked behind Hormuz, the math does not work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Restricted Silver Imports for the Second Time in a Month. The $12 Billion Bill Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: Silver in grain and powder form now requires prior government approval. India spent a record $12 billion importing the metal last year — more than double the previous year — and the rupee cannot afford it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Faces Its Hardest Rate Call in Years. The Iran War, a Sinking Rupee and a Failing Monsoon All Want Different Things.
articles.excerpt: Nearly 80% of economists expect the central bank to hold rates at 5.25% on Friday, but interest rate swaps are pricing in 100 basis points of tightening over the next year. Something has to give.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Just Put His Housing Regulator in Charge of 18 Spy Agencies. The CIA Was Already at War With Itself.
articles.excerpt: Bill Pulte, who has no intelligence experience, replaces the departing Tulsi Gabbard as acting DNI while the US is fighting Iran, the CIA has stopped cooperating with its oversight body, and oil prices are at a one-week high.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's UPI Just Processed 23.2 Billion Transactions in a Single Month. That Is More Than Visa Handles in an Entire Quarter.
articles.excerpt: Driven by IPL fever and summer travel, India's homegrown payment rails hit ₹29.9 lakh crore in May — and the system is now live in seven countries, including the UAE and Singapore.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Lowered Its Foodgrain Production Target for the First Time in Years. El Niño Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: The government set a target of 373.93 million tonnes for 2026-27 — down from last year's record 376.56 million tonnes — as IMD predicts below-normal monsoon rainfall.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Reversed Course on the Global Vaccine Alliance. India Had Already Pledged $20 Million.
articles.excerpt: Rubio told Congress the State Department would re-engage with Gavi after a year-long funding freeze — a move driven by the Ebola outbreak and bipartisan pressure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UNICEF Says the Iran War Is Now Delaying Lifesaving Aid to Children by Up to Six Months
articles.excerpt: Surging transport costs, port congestion, and shipping reroutes have nearly exhausted the agency's annual flight donations in a single quarter — with the Ebola response in Congo adding to the strain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran's Hormuz Toll Authority Says 300 Ships Have Applied for Safe Passage. Most Want to Reach India and China.
articles.excerpt: The Persian Gulf Strait Authority, now under US sanctions, says 77% of applicants are oil tankers heading to Asia — but Washington has told vessels not to pay.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Supreme Court Just Hit Its Highest-Ever Strength. One of the New Judges Was Never a Judge Before.
articles.excerpt: Five judges took oath on Tuesday, bringing the court to 37 — including V. Mohana, only the second woman in India's history to be elevated directly from the Bar to the apex court.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 17-Year-Old Read CBSE's Tender Files. Now India Has a New Board Chairman.
articles.excerpt: The government replaced the CBSE chief and secretary within hours after a student's analysis of the On-Screen Marking contract triggered a national firestorm.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Venezuela's Acting President Will Visit India This Week. The Oil Math Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: Delcy Rodriguez arrives Wednesday for five days of energy talks as India becomes the second-largest buyer of Venezuelan crude, importing 427,000 barrels a day.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Abu Dhabi's Oil Giant Just Found a Way Around the Hormuz Blockade. It Goes Through Oman.
articles.excerpt: ADNOC has resumed naphtha exports by shuttling cargoes from its refinery inside the Gulf to Oman's Sohar port for ship-to-ship transfer — a workaround that could ease Asia's energy crunch.
articles.nri_angle: India imports over 80% of its crude oil, and the Hormuz closure has forced a rapid reorientation of supply chains. Indian refiners like Reliance and Indian Oil need alternative feedstock routes. The newly activated India-Oman CEPA strengthens this alternative corridor. Oil at $93/barrel and the rupee at 95.26 per dollar directly impact NRI remittances and household costs in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Is About to Become the Largest IPO in History. The Number Is $1.75 Trillion.
articles.excerpt: Elon Musk's rocket, satellite and AI conglomerate will raise at least $75 billion when it lists on the Nasdaq on June 12. Morningstar says the company is worth less than half that.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers form a significant share of SpaceX's workforce, especially in Starlink and propulsion. Indian retail investors increasingly accessing US markets through liberalised remittance and fractional-share platforms. Starlink's pending broadband spectrum application in India could gain momentum. India's own space startups — Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel — face questions about competitiveness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Issues Ebola Advisory as WHO Declares the Outbreak a Global Health Emergency
articles.excerpt: No cases reported in India yet, but the health ministry is urging travellers from Central Africa to self-monitor for 21 days as the Bundibugyo strain spreads across borders.
articles.nri_angle: An estimated 100,000 Indians live and work across sub-Saharan Africa, including in Uganda, Kenya, and the DRC — all directly affected by the outbreak. India's pharma supply chains to Africa face potential disruption. NRI travellers transiting through Central Africa face new screening and isolation requirements.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Monsoon Forecast Just Got Worse. It Could Be the Driest Season in 11 Years.
articles.excerpt: IMD now expects rainfall at just 90 per cent of normal — down from an already cautious 92 per cent — as an emerging El Niño threatens crops, reservoirs, and food prices across the subcontinent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Supreme Court Just Upheld a 28% Tax on Every Rupee Bet on Online Games. The Bill Could Exceed ₹1 Lakh Crore.
articles.excerpt: The ruling validates retrospective GST demands on Dream11, MPL, and over 100 gaming companies, ending a legal battle that goes back to the industry's earliest days.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is About to Launch a Producer Price Index for the First Time. It Will Replace a System the Country Has Used for Decades.
articles.excerpt: The new PPI will track inflation in services — including banking, railways, and telecom — for the first time, bringing India in line with global statistical standards after two decades of debate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and the US Are Now in the Final Hours of a Trade Deal. The Ambassador Says It Is 99% Done.
articles.excerpt: A three-day negotiating round in New Delhi could produce the first bilateral trade agreement between the world's largest and fifth-largest economies. The sticking point is Section 301.
articles.nri_angle: A strengthened India-US trade corridor means more business opportunities, easier capital flows, and deeper strategic alignment for the 4.5 million Indian Americans. India's $500 billion purchase commitment over five years — covering energy, aircraft, and tech — could reshape job markets and investment patterns on both sides of the Pacific.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Is Now Reviewing the Text of a Deal to End the War. Trump Says It Will Be Done Within a Week.
articles.excerpt: After freezing talks on Monday, Tehran reversed course within hours. Oil prices fell 1% on Tuesday, but the IEA warns global inventories could hit historic lows.
articles.nri_angle: India's Finance Ministry has called the Hormuz disruption the single most consequential variable for the country's external balance. Gulf oil imports are down 34%. Even a best-case deal would not deliver relief to Indian consumers until late October. The RBI faces pressure to raise rates to defend the rupee, and the current account deficit is widening. For NRIs sending money home, the rupee's trajectory is directly tied to this conflict.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 25-Year-Old Keralite Delta Pilot Was Killed in a Helicopter Crash Hours After His Wedding. His Bride Survived.
articles.excerpt: Dave Fiji, a first officer at Delta Air Lines, had warned the pilot about zero visibility before takeoff. His wife Jesni was trapped in the wreckage for six hours.
articles.nri_angle: Dave Fiji's parents emigrated from Muvattupuzha in Ernakulam, Kerala. His wife Jesni's family hails from Alappuzha. The couple met through the Keralite church community in Georgia. The tragedy has shaken the Indian American community in Atlanta and beyond — a story of an immigrant family's American dream cut short on the happiest day of their son's life.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Dropped to Seventh in Global Market Cap Rankings. South Korea's AI Chip Boom Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: In 18 months, India went from a market cap three-and-a-half times South Korea's to being overtaken. Foreign investors have pulled $26.4 billion this year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New Trade Deal With Oman Just Went Live. It May Be the Country's Most Important FTA This Decade.
articles.excerpt: The CEPA gives 99% of Indian exports duty-free access and secures $7.2 billion in energy imports — right as the Strait of Hormuz remains under threat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rubio Will Testify in Public for the First Time on the Iran War This Week. His Own Party Wants Answers.
articles.excerpt: Republicans are asking about strategy, gasoline prices and an exit plan. Democrats say the war should end 'no matter the terms at this point.'
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Goldman Sachs Just Named India the Most Vulnerable Major Economy on Earth. The Number Is 3.6%.
articles.excerpt: A new Goldman analysis maps exactly how much economic damage the Hormuz blockade can inflict country by country — and India tops the list, above Turkey, South Korea, and every G7 nation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Quietly Rewiring Its Entire Oil Supply Chain. Venezuela Is Now Its Fourth-Largest Supplier.
articles.excerpt: Three months into the Hormuz blockade, Indian refiners have shifted billions of dollars in crude purchases to Latin America and Africa — a move that looks less like a stopgap and more like a permanent realignment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Blackstone-Backed Firm Just Committed $21 Billion to Build a Data Centre on the Outskirts of Mumbai.
articles.excerpt: AirTrunk's deal in Maharashtra is part of a $630 billion wave of tech investments that is turning India into Asia's AI infrastructure hub — and the biggest construction site the cloud industry has ever seen.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russia Just Launched 656 Drones and 73 Missiles at Ukraine in a Single Night. At Least 11 Are Dead.
articles.excerpt: The assault on Kyiv, Dnipro, and Kharkiv included eight Zircon hypersonic missiles — the largest single use of the weapon in the war. Poland scrambled jets. Oil climbed again. India stayed silent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Just Met Myanmar's Military Ruler in New Delhi. The West Wanted India to Isolate Him.
articles.excerpt: Min Aung Hlaing's first visit to India since becoming president drew sharp criticism from human rights groups. India said engagement works better than isolation. The 1,643-km border is the reason.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump's Own Party Just Killed His $1.8 Billion 'Weaponization' Fund. It Was the Price of Getting His Border Bill Passed.
articles.excerpt: Senate Republicans refused to move on $72 billion in immigration enforcement funding until the White House agreed to scrap a fund critics called a slush fund for January 6 defendants. Mitch McConnell called it 'utterly stupid, morally wrong.'
articles.nri_angle: The ICE and Border Patrol funding package — stalled by this controversy — includes provisions affecting visa processing times, asylum adjudication and workplace enforcement for the estimated 4.4 million Indian Americans navigating the US immigration system.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Have Now Pulled More Money Out of India in 2026 Than They Did in All of 2025.
articles.excerpt: It took them just five months. The $26.4 billion exodus — driven by the Iran war, $94 oil and a weak monsoon forecast — has surpassed last year's full-year record of $18.91 billion and shows no sign of slowing.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with investments in Indian equities or considering fund repatriation face a key decision point as the rupee weakens toward 95-100 and RBI burns forex reserves. The Q1 GDP data and RBI decision on Friday will shape NRI investment strategy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Threatened to Pull the Scotch Whisky Tariff Cut. Britain's Steel Restrictions Are the Reason.
articles.excerpt: A year-old trade deal that promised to reshape commerce between the world's fifth- and sixth-largest economies is unravelling before it has even taken effect. Britain's Trade Secretary is in New Delhi today to try to fix it.
articles.nri_angle: The India-UK trade deal includes enhanced mobility provisions, qualification recognition and visa pathways for Indian professionals in the UK — all now hostage to a steel dispute. The 1.8 million-strong Indian diaspora in Britain and Indian students face uncertainty.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every Country at the Shangri-La Dialogue Had the Same Message. Arm Yourself. And Find Partners Who Will Arm With You.
articles.excerpt: Asia's premier defence summit ended with a clear takeaway: Indo-Pacific nations are racing to deepen security ties with each other — not because the US is leaving, but because they are no longer sure it will stay.

sources.label: Ministry of Defence, Government of India

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lebanon Just Announced a Partial Ceasefire Between Israel and Hezbollah. Nobody Has Stopped Fighting.
articles.excerpt: The deal calls on Israel to spare Beirut while Hezbollah halts attacks on Israel. Southern Lebanon remains a war zone. Iran says there is no separate peace — any ceasefire must cover all fronts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Australia Just Agreed to Map Each Other's Oceans. A Joint Rescue Drill in Chennai Will Start This Month.
articles.excerpt: At their second Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, Rajnath Singh and Richard Marles signed off on a maritime roadmap, a new defence equipment MoU, and deeper undersea surveillance cooperation.

sources.label: Ministry of Defence, Government of India

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Signed a BrahMos Deal With Vietnam. Three Southeast Asian Nations Now Carry the Missile.
articles.excerpt: Defence exports hit a record ₹38,424 crore as Operation Sindoor drives unprecedented global demand for Indian weapons systems.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Sent France the Paperwork for 114 Rafale Jets. The Bill Is ₹3.25 Lakh Crore.
articles.excerpt: The Letter of Request for the country's largest-ever defence acquisition comes weeks before Modi's expected visit to Paris. Ninety-four of the jets will be built in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Defence Secretary Just Called India a 'Powerful' Military Nation. He Said It at Asia's Top Security Forum.
articles.excerpt: Pete Hegseth praised India's military modernisation and industrial capacity at the Shangri-La Dialogue while calling on Asian allies to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Alphabet Just Announced the Largest Equity Raise in Tech History. Berkshire Hathaway Is Buying $10 Billion.
articles.excerpt: Google's parent company will sell $80 billion in stock to fund AI data centres. Warren Buffett's successor endorsed the bet with a massive private placement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Told India's Exam Agency to Learn From the One Body That Has Never Had a Paper Leak.
articles.excerpt: NEET UG 2026 was cancelled after a widespread paper leak. 23 lakh students must retake it on June 21. The court wants the NTA to explain how this keeps happening.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Just Jumped $5 in a Single Day. An Exxon Executive Says Prices Could Hit $160.
articles.excerpt: Brent crude surged past $95 after Iran threatened to block two of the world's most important shipping lanes. Exxon warned that global inventories are approaching unheard of lows.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Meets This Week. Every Economist Expects It to Do Nothing. That May Be the Point.
articles.excerpt: The central bank is expected to hold rates at 5.25 percent on Friday. But with oil above $90, the rupee near 95, and inflation rising, the real signal will be in what it says next.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Car Sales Just Hit an All-Time High. The Iran War Is the Reason People Are Buying CNG.
articles.excerpt: Maruti Suzuki sold more cars in a single month than ever before. Its CNG bookings jumped 40 percent after four fuel price hikes in May.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's President Just Appointed Five New Supreme Court Judges. The Court Is Racing to Clear a Backlog of Over 80,000 Cases.
articles.excerpt: The appointments follow the Collegium's May 22 and May 27 recommendations and include four High Court chief justices and one senior advocate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
